text:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout promptmux-v2 (quantized) canary 5% -> 20% across us-east-1/us-west-2

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: latency_p99 > SLO (streaming.generate) — triggered at 5044440020 — paging ops team

maya: saw it on dashboard, p99 jumped from ~220ms -> ~1.6s at 5044440000-5044440020

jordan: noticing streaming stalls too, clients reporting chunk gaps, p95 also climbed ~300ms

samir: @maya can you drop the short query that shows p95/p99 and active streams? might help scope

maya: copying query
```
avg_over_time(latency_ms{route="/v1/stream"}[2m]) by (quantile)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

maya: results: p95 ~380ms, p99 ~1.6s, active streams 420 -> 1800 since canary started

ops-sre: looks correlated with canary traffic bump. traffic to promptmux-v2 went from 5% -> 20% at 5044440000

leah: is this the quantized path? we had a kernel change in that build for KV handling

jordan: yes, quant path uses new KV warmup + compact kernel. suspect KV miss storm + blocking IO

samir: customer-ops can we surface if any customer-facing errors? maybe retries from SDKs causing head-of-line

customer-ops: two enterprise customers reported streaming stalls and reconnects, one logged increased latency warnings

ops-sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) shift canary back to 5% 2) abort and rollback 3) enable fallback model variant for streaming

leah: can we hotfix kernel? risky during incident. I'd prefer rollback to known-good variant for safety

maya: agree. shift traffic back to 5% first to buy time. I can update routing policy

deploy-bot: Canary traffic update: applying routing change -> canary weight 10% (in progress)

jordan: monitoring... p99 dropping but still elevated at ~900ms

deploy-bot: Canary traffic update: applied -> canary weight 5%

maya: p99 trending down to 320ms now, streaming stalls reduced, active streams 540

samir: ok confirm: do we want to fully rollback or proceed with canary pause + deeper triage?

leah: pause rollout and mark the deployment aborted. Do not re-escalate traffic until root cause found

maya: executing abort
```
/deploy abort promptmux-v2 --reason "canary tail latency spike; pause for triage" 
```

deploy-bot: Abort acknowledged. Initiating canary freeze and traffic convergence to baseline model (promptmux-v1)

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-504444001 — Canary-induced streaming tail latency. Severity: sev2. Incident lead: ops-sre

ops-sre: I'm taking lead. Task list: 1) collect kernel logs from affected nodes 2) gather KV cache miss rates 3) reproduce with a replay of canary traffic 4) customer impact summary

jordan: I'll take replay and perf harness. starting a warmup test to isolate kv miss behavior

samir: I'll prep customer impact note for support + notifications. quick note: two customers saw reconnects, one had background retry loops.

customer-ops: customers notified: status page patch and support DMs in progress. No major data loss; degraded streaming UX reported.

leah: ask infra to snapshot one of the affected GPUs before rebooting anything, we need traces

ops-sre: noted. adding: escalate to eng-runtime if kernel-level repro occurs

maya: adding traces: sample traces show blocking time inside kv_lookup() during first 7 tokens of streams

jordan: replay harness shows heavy KV miss rate when concurrency spikes past ~800 active streams; warmup reduces misses but rollout timing overlapped with traffic spike

ops-sre: preliminary RCA hypothesis: quantized kernel interacts poorly with cold KV cache under multiplexed streaming load -> temporary tail latency surge and stalls

leah: next steps: revert kernel change on the build or disable quantized kernel path for streaming-only endpoints

ops-sre: short term: keep canary frozen and schedule rollback of quant kernel to v1 in the next patch release. Long term: improve KV warmup and safer rollout gating (ramp based on active_streams metric)

samir: drafting post-incident note and customer impact summary. will include mitigation steps and timeline

oncall-bot: Paging cleared: latency_p99 recovered under threshold at 5044440352 — incident remains open for triage

ops-sre: handoff to morning oncall for follow-up. leaving this thread open for any late customer reports

leah: thumbs up. I’ll open a follow-up RFC for rollout gating + probe-based canary policy

maya: thanks everyone. I’ll attach dashboards and trace snippets to the incident ticket.

customer-ops: customers will be updated when we have timeline for kernel patch; keeping watch for regressions

jordan: final note: avoid simultaneous canary ramp + synthetic traffic bursts in the future, we need a guardrail

samir: logging timeline into INC-504444001 notes. will link to PR and perf runs.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket updated: INC-504444001 — canary paused, rollback planned, owners assigned

maya: closing chat for now. available if paging fires again. :eyes:
